findings.title: Dataclass default `queued` is evaluated once at class definition, not per-instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field with a plain default value, which Python evaluates exactly once when the class body is executed (at import time), not each time an `AssignmentSource` instance is constructed. Every `AssignmentSource` created without explicitly passing `queued` (e.g. via `from_integration()`, which is the only construction path used in production code) will therefore share the exact same stale timestamp from process start, instead of reflecting when the assignment was actually queued. This should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead. As written, any logic that later relies on `queued` to reason about staleness/ordering will be silently wrong.

findings.title: Raw datetime embedded in task kwargs may not survive Celery serialization
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `dataclasses.asdict`) includes the raw `queued: datetime` field, and this dict is passed directly as a kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={...})`. Depending on the task's serializer, a native `datetime` object inside a dict may not be JSON-serializable, which could cause the task enqueue to fail (or require a custom encoder) in production. Because tests use `self.tasks()` (synchronous/eager execution), this potential serialization failure would not be exercised by the current test suite, so there's no coverage proving the AssignmentSource survives real task queuing.

findings.title: No test exercising the "different integration" propagation path
findings.body: The new `should_sync` logic in `mixins/issues.py` is explicitly designed to still propagate outbound sync when the `AssignmentSource` originates from a *different* integration than the one being evaluated (per the inline comment: "This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward"). The only new test (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`) covers the same-integration (blocked) case; there is no test asserting that a non-matching `AssignmentSource` (e.g. assignment source from Integration A, sync check on Integration B) still results in `sync_assignee_outbound` being called. This is the core multi-integration guarantee of the fix and is currently unverified.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to `sync_status_outbound` abstract signature but never wired up
findings.body: The abstract method `sync_status_outbound` now accepts an `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None` parameter, matching the pattern used for assignee sync, but no caller in this PR (or in the shown diffs) actually constructs/passes an `AssignmentSource` into `sync_status_outbound`. The status-sync task/pipeline isn't touched, so the parameter is dead for now. If the intent was to also prevent status sync cycles, this is incomplete; if not, the signature change is premature and may confuse implementers of `IssueSyncIntegration` subclasses who now need to accept a parameter that's never populated.
